newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef was generally lower on fairly good demand and moderate to heavy offerings, USDA said. Retail demand again was for their immediate needs, and forward interest continued rather slow.

Rib cuts were under pressure all week, with the most weakness on the Select cuts. Chuck and round cuts traded generally lower. The round cuts were under the most downward pressure, especially the Select cuts, which traded lower as the week progressed. Loin cuts started the week trading at firmer price levels, but as the week progressed, both the light Select and Choice cuts were trading lower.

Closely trimmed items also were under pressure, and again the Select cuts traded lower. Beef trimmings were generally steady for the week on moderate demand and offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 1.00 to 1.50 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.00 to 1.50 lower; Select and Choice round primal 2.00 to 3.50 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 1.00 to 2.00 lower; Closely trimmed items 1.50 to 2.00 lower; Beef trimmings generally steady; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.44 at 105.45; 700/850 Dn 1.18 at 105.20; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 2.07 at 100.05; 700/850 Dn 1.75 at 99.73.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The lean boneless beef market struggled this week after several weeks of steady to firm price levels. Sellers were forced to clean up inventories at sharply lower levels in order to stay current.

In addition, live cow prices showed weakness this week, and in return the cow carcasses market declined slightly. Moreover, demand for 100% lean items remained good and prices continued to be firm but leveled off compared to recent weeks. However, ribeye rolls traded lower, as seasonal demand shifted to a lip-on ribeye roll.

Utility carcasses 1.00 lower; Cutter not established; 90% boneless beef 9.00-9.50 lower; 85% 6.00-8.00 lower; 75% mostly 2.50 lower; 65% steady. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, April 24, 1997 was estimated at 78.52 per cwt., down 5.35 from a week ago
